attestation.payload: the attestation object with its "signature" member removed (every other member is signed)

signing.key_id_derivation: first 16 lowercase hex chars of sha256(raw 32-byte public key)
signing.key_source: Use keys[] of this document fetched from a URL you trust (never issuer.issuer_url from the attestation), and pin the expected key_id. signature.public_key_b64 is informational only and MUST NOT be used for verification.
signing.on_failure: Stop at the first failing check and report its name.
signing.public_key_encoding: keys[].public_key_b64: standard base64 (RFC 4648, padded) of the raw 32-byte Ed25519 public key
signing.retired_at: Present only on keys with status "retired": RFC 3339 UTC YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Active keys have no retired_at. Valid iff issued_at <= retired_at.
signing.signature_encoding: signature.value_b64: standard base64 (RFC 4648, padded) of the 64-byte Ed25519 signature

verify: Check order: run the checks below in this order and stop at the first failure, reporting that step number and name (the official verifiers do the same). All checks apply to an attestation; snapshot meta uses only steps 5, 6 and 9 (with its own prefix).
1 spec_version_canonicalization: require spec == "prepay-check-attestation", version == "1.0" and canonicalization == "JCS".

2 signature_block: signature must be an object with alg == "Ed25519" and value_b64 a string. signature.public_key_b64 is informational only: a verifier MUST NOT use it for verification and MUST take the key from keys[] of this document (or from a key pinned out of band).

3 pinned_key_id: mandatory; pin the expected key_id (or fingerprint) from a source you trust and require signature.key_id to equal it. Never take the issuer document or key from issuer.issuer_url inside the attestation: whoever made the attestation chose that URL.
5 key_lookup: require exactly one entry in keys[] with key_id == signature.key_id.
6 key_integrity: keys[].public_key_b64 is standard base64 of the raw 32-byte Ed25519 public key; require 32 bytes and key_id == first 16 lowercase hex chars of sha256(raw key).
7 validity_window: issued_at and expires_at must be UTC timestamps YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ (second precision); require 0 <= expires_at - issued_at <= 86400 s.

8 key_not_retired: keys[].status is "active" or "retired". The active key has no retired_at member. A retired key has retired_at (RFC 3339 UTC, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ). The attestation is valid only if issued_at <= retired_at (an attestation issued exactly at retired_at is still accepted); reject if issued_at > retired_at or if retired_at is missing or unparseable.

9 signature: payload = attestation without its "signature" member (snapshot meta: the "metadata" member); message = UTF-8 of signing_prefix (attestation: "prepay-check-attestation/v1" + LF, hex 7072657061792d636865636b2d6174746573746174696f6e2f76310a; snapshot meta: "bazaar-snapshot-meta/v1" + LF) followed by RFC 8785 (JCS) of the payload as UTF-8. Verify signature.value_b64 (standard base64, 64 bytes) over the message with Ed25519 (RFC 8032). Without the prefix the signature does not verify.
10 not_future: reject if issued_at > now + 60 s.

# Base Reads

> Pay-per-call read API for Base mainnet over x402 v2. Each paid route answers GET without payment with HTTP 402 and a PAYMENT-REQUIRED challenge; retry with a PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header to get JSON.

## Payment

- Protocol: x402 v2, scheme exact
- Network: eip155:8453 (Base mainnet)
- Asset: USDC 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913
- Authorization: EIP-3009 transferWithAuthorization only (Permit2 is rejected)
- Responses are served only after the transfer is confirmed on-chain
- Optional ?ref=<tag> (A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ -, max 64) is recorded for attribution and never changes price or challenge

## Paid routes (GET, JSON)

- /base/usdc-balance (0.001 USDC): Live Base mainnet USDC and ETH balance for one address, read with eth_call at the latest block; returns decimal and raw values plus the block number. Use it to check a wallet can cover a payment or that funds arrived before acting. Simpler than running an RPC client and decoding ERC-20 calls yourself, and the block number makes each reading reproducible. Query: ?address=0x...
- /base/tx-status (0.002 USDC): Base mainnet transaction status: success, failed or pending, with block, confirmations, gas used, effective gas price, from/to and log count. Use it after sending or receiving a payment to confirm it landed and how deep it is. One normalized JSON answer instead of combining receipt and block calls and computing confirmations yourself. Query: ?hash=0x...
- /base/basename (0.003 USDC): Resolve a Basename (name.base.eth) to its Base address, or an address to its primary Basename, checked both ways so a reverse name is only returned when it resolves back. Use it to turn a human name into a payout address or to label an address. Avoids hand-written ENS-style namehash and resolver calls. Query: ?name=jesse.base.eth or ?address=0x...
- /base/address-intel (0.010 USDC): One call for an address on Base: USDC balance, ETH balance, verified primary Basename, transaction count (nonce) and whether it is a contract. Use it to profile a counterparty or payout wallet before interacting. Replaces four or five separate reads with a single priced request. Query: ?address=0x...
- /x402/preflight (0.010 USDC): Pre-pay Check: Ed25519-signed, deterministic facts about another x402 endpoint before you pay it: challenge validity, reachability and latency, host listing count, payout wallet reuse across hosts, last-called and payer trend from daily Bazaar snapshots. Use it when choosing between paid endpoints. Signed facts you can verify against the published key, not ratings; facts only, no advice. Query: ?url=https://...
- /base/network (0.001 USDC): Base mainnet head: latest block number, block age in seconds, base fee and gas price in gwei. Use it to check the chain is advancing and to estimate fees before sending a transaction. One small JSON read instead of several raw RPC calls and unit conversions.

## What the responses are

- Verifiable facts only: /base/network, /base/usdc-balance, /base/address-intel and /base/tx-status (once mined) include the Base block number they refer to, so those readings can be reproduced against any Base RPC node
- No verdicts, opinions, scores or predictions, no buy/sell advice, and no language model in the response path
- Compared with a free RPC endpoint: values are normalized (decimal and raw units, gwei, confirmations), pinned to a block number, and several reads are combined into one call

## Usage pattern

- To get signed facts about an x402 endpoint before paying it, you can call /x402/preflight?url=<endpoint> (0.010 USDC). Facts only, no guarantee.
- /base/network and /base/usdc-balance responses list related_routes (path and price) for follow-up reads

## Discovery (free)

- / : service index with routes and prices
- /openapi.json : OpenAPI 3.1 description of the paid routes with prices
- /bazaar/snapshots : daily Bazaar snapshot summary
- /.well-known/bazaar-snapshot.json : signed snapshot series metadata
- /.well-known/x402-preflight : Pre-pay Check schema and signing key
- /.well-known/x402-preflight-key-history.json : signing key history
- /.well-known/issuer.json : attestation issuer, contact and signing keys (active and retired), plus machine-readable signing rules and verify steps. v1.0 attestation: Ed25519 (RFC 8032) over UTF-8 of "prepay-check-attestation/v1" + LF followed by RFC 8785 (JCS) of the attestation without its signature member; snapshot meta uses the prefix "bazaar-snapshot-meta/v1" + LF
- /.well-known/prepay-check-attestation-v1.schema.json : JSON Schema of the signed attestation (CC0)
- /x402/preflight/pubkey : Ed25519 public key for verifying signed facts
- Each 402 challenge carries extensions.bazaar (input schema and output example) for x402 Bazaar listing

Facts only, no investment advice.
